key_insight: Antidistillation Fingerprinting embeds subtle, optimized signals into a teacher LLM so that those signals reliably survive a wide range of distillation procedures, enabling detection of student models trained on the teacher without noticeably degrading generation quality.
problem_solved: Detecting when third-party student models were trained on a teacher's outputs while avoiding the steep quality-vs.-detectability trade-offs of prior heuristic fingerprinting or watermarking techniques.
method: Optimize compact, low-visibility fingerprint signals injected into teacher outputs that create persistent distributional artifacts rather than obvious token-level perturbations.
Train or regularize the teacher (or its inference outputs) with an objective that maximizes detectability under typical distillation pipelines while constraining downstream utility loss.
Evaluate robustness with simulated distillation scenarios and statistical detectors applied to student generations to measure persistence and false-positive rates.
impact: Provides model owners and practitioners a practical way to establish provenance and detect unauthorized distillation of LLMs with minimal impact on model quality, aiding licensing enforcement and model accountability.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Teacher -> Distillation -> Student showing fingerprint signal surviving through training
Trade-off chart: detectability vs generation quality comparing prior heuristics to the antidistillation method
ROC/precision-recall curve showing detection performance across distillation variants
Annotated example generation highlighting the imperceptible fingerprint features in teacher output vs student output
paper_authors: Yixuan Even Xu, John Kirchenbauer, Yash Savani, Asher Trockman, Alexander Robey
